actions.Alert: Accept the request and generate an alert email and/or log message; traffic passes to the server unchanged.
actions.alert: Accept the request and generate an alert email and/or log message; traffic passes to the server unchanged.
actions.Alert & Deny: Block the request (or reset the connection) and generate an alert email and/or log message; the block page/HTTP status code returned to the client is customizable via replacement messages.
actions.alert_deny: Block the request (or reset the connection) and generate an alert email and/or log message; the block page/HTTP status code returned to the client is customizable via replacement messages.
actions.Deny (no log): Block the request (or reset the connection) without generating any alert email or log message.
actions.deny_no_log: Block the request (or reset the connection) without generating any alert email or log message.
actions.Period Block: Block all subsequent requests from that client source IP for the configured Block Period (typically 1-3600 s; 1-600 s for IP List/Geo IP, up to 10000 s for HTTP Access Limit/API Gateway); behind a NAT load balancer you MUST configure an X-header with the real client IP or FortiWeb may block ALL connections.
actions.block-period: Block all subsequent requests from that client source IP for the configured Block Period (typically 1-3600 s; 1-600 s for IP List/Geo IP, up to 10000 s for HTTP Access Limit/API Gateway); behind a NAT load balancer you MUST configure an X-header with the real client IP or FortiWeb may block ALL connections.
actions.Client ID Block Period: Block the client for N seconds based on the FortiWeb-generated client ID (Client Management) instead of source IP; useful when the client's source IP keeps changing.
actions.client-id-block-period: Block the client for N seconds based on the FortiWeb-generated client ID (Client Management) instead of source IP; useful when the client's source IP keeps changing.
actions.Redirect: Redirect the request to the Redirect URL configured in the protection profile and generate an alert/log; optionally appends the violation reason as a URL parameter (e.g. reason747sha=Parameter%20Validation%20Violation) and redirect491=1 to break redirect loops.
actions.redirect: Redirect the request to the Redirect URL configured in the protection profile and generate an alert/log; optionally appends the violation reason as a URL parameter (e.g. reason747sha=Parameter%20Validation%20Violation) and redirect491=1 to break redirect loops.
actions.Send HTTP Response: Block the request and reply to the client with a customizable HTTP error message/error code, and generate an alert email and/or log message.
actions.send_http_response: Block the request and reply to the client with a customizable HTTP error message/error code, and generate an alert email and/or log message.
actions.Send 403 Forbidden: Reply to the client with an HTTP 403 Access Forbidden error message and generate an alert email and/or log message.
actions.send_403_forbidden: Reply to the client with an HTTP 403 Access Forbidden error message and generate an alert email and/or log message.
actions.Alert & Erase: Response-side cloaking: hide sensitive information in replies from the web server - block the request or remove (erase) the sensitive data from the response - and generate an alert/log. Not fully supported in Offline Protection mode (there only alert/log is possible; data cannot be blocked or erased).
actions.alert_erase: Response-side cloaking: hide sensitive information in replies from the web server - block the request or remove (erase) the sensitive data from the response - and generate an alert/log. Not fully supported in Offline Protection mode (there only alert/log is possible; data cannot be blocked or erased).
actions.Erase, no Alert: Same response cloaking as Alert & Erase but without generating any alert email or log message; not supported at all in Offline Protection mode.
actions.only_erase: Same response cloaking as Alert & Erase but without generating any alert email or log message; not supported at all in Offline Protection mode.
actions.Pass: Allow the request; do not generate any alert or log message (URL Access rules; default action there).
actions.pass: Allow the request; do not generate any alert or log message (URL Access rules; default action there).
actions.Continue: Continue evaluating subsequent rules in the web protection profile (Sequence of scans); if no other rule is violated the request is allowed; a single request violating multiple rules generates multiple attack log messages.
actions.continue: Continue evaluating subsequent rules in the web protection profile (Sequence of scans); if no other rule is violated the request is allowed; a single request violating multiple rules generates multiple attack log messages.
actions.Bypass: Accept the request (Known Bots): the matched bot traffic is let through (and for Known Good Bots it also skips the subsequent scans after Known Bots).
actions.bypass: Accept the request (Known Bots): the matched bot traffic is let through (and for Known Good Bots it also skips the subsequent scans after Known Bots).
actions.Remove Cookie: Accept the request but strip the offending cookie from the datagram before it reaches the web server, and generate an alert/log (Cookie Security only).
actions.remove_cookie: Accept the request but strip the offending cookie from the datagram before it reaches the web server, and generate an alert/log (Cookie Security only).
actions.Alert Only (FortiGuard-enhanced signatur: When FortiGuard updates enhance an existing signature, its action automatically switches to Alert Only until you Approve it in System > Config > FortiGuard > Signature Update Management, even if the policy configured a blocking action.
actions.alert_only: When FortiGuard updates enhance an existing signature, its action automatically switches to Alert Only until you Approve it in System > Config > FortiGuard > Signature Update Management, even if the policy configured a blocking action.
actions._monitor_mode_caveat: On nearly every feature page: 'This setting will be ignored if Monitor Mode is enabled' - in Monitor Mode FortiWeb only logs; no blocking/erasing/redirecting happens.

signatures.what: FortiGuard-updated (plus custom) attack signatures scan URL parameters, POST body parameters, XML/JSON body, cookies, headers and uploaded filenames for XSS, SQL injection, generic attacks (LFI/RFI/command injection), trojans/webshells, information disclosure, bad robots, and personally identifiable information. Each category (and each individual signature) has its own action, severity and trigger; a Signature Wizard can generate a policy with irrelevant signatures disabled; a Sensitivity Level adds/removes signatures.
signatures.backend_reaction: Per-category action: request passes with log (Alert), is blocked/reset with customizable block page (Alert & Deny, Deny no log, Send HTTP Response), client is IP-blocked 1-3600 s (Period Block), redirected, or for response-side categories (Information Disclosure, PII) the response is rewritten to erase the sensitive data (Alert & Erase / Erase no Alert; Offline mode can only log, not erase). All ignored in Monitor Mode. WebSocket traffic: only alert/period-block/deny are really executed.
regex_fields: Custom signatures are regex-based (see Defining custom data leak & attack signatures)
Signature exceptions / action overrides: Host, URI, Full URL, Parameter name/value, Cookie name/value when Operation = Regular Expression Match

examples.note: Log format: category, subtype and signature ID.
Trigger only when a page contains >= 2 instances of PII (range 1-128).

gotchas: Extended categories (XSS/SQLi/Generic Extended) are more false-positive prone
Information Disclosure / PII require a decompression rule and (for HTTPS) the server certificate, otherwise the scan is effectively disabled
Info Disclosure can rewrite every response - performance cost; Fortinet suggests using it only for logging until servers are fixed
FortiGuard-enhanced signatures auto-switch to Alert Only until Approved
Individual signatures can be disabled per-policy or in all policies (right-click in Signature Details)
Scanning limited by HTTP-cachesize buffer; disable HTTP Return Code 4XX/5XX signatures to reduce noise
False Positive Mitigation adds SQL syntax validation to SQLi signatures

http_constraints.what: Enforces RFC/buffer limits on the HTTP protocol itself: content length, header count/name/value lengths, parameter count/length/illegal-null characters, illegal method/version/hostname/content-type, malformed requests and parser buffer overflows, HTTP/2 SETTINGS limits (table size, streams, window, frame, header list, RST-stream floods), cookies count, Range header count, chunk size, RPC and WebSocket protocol detection. Prevents buffer-overflow style attacks.
http_constraints.backend_reaction: Per-constraint action: log only (Alert), block/reset with customizable page (Alert & Deny), silent block (Deny no log), or IP block for 1-3600 s (Period Block). Ignored in Monitor Mode. Bypassed entirely if the source IP is a configured Known Search Engine.
regex_fields: Exception rule URL Pattern when Request Type = Regular Expression

Exceptions are matched by URL and only the FIRST matching exception rule is applied (e.g. /example/* rule shadows a later /example/abc rule)
Number of URL Parameters max 1024; Ranges-in-Range-header default 5 (Apache DoS)
Per-constraint Threat Weight when Client Management is enabled
Some constraints apply only to HTTP/1.x or only to HTTP/2
Exceptions can also be scoped by Host and Source IP

allow_method.what: Whitelist of allowed HTTP request methods (GET, POST, HEAD, PUT, DELETE, TRACE, OPTIONS, PATCH, WEBDAV, OTHERS...) per protection profile, with per-host/per-URL exceptions that allow different method sets. OTHERS covers any custom/non-standard method. Optional Override Header/Override Parameter check also validates methods smuggled in headers/parameters.
allow_method.backend_reaction: Methods not selected are denied (request blocked) unless an Allow Method Exception matching the Host/URL allows them; violations are logged with the configured Severity and Trigger Policy.
actions_available: (implicit deny of unselected methods; Severity + Trigger Policy configurable)

ip_list.what: Per-policy list of client source IPs/ranges classified as Block IP (always blocked), Trust IP (skips many later scans), or Allow Only (anything outside the range is blocked). Supports single IPs, comma-separated ranges (IPv4/IPv6), IP Groups, and external IP connectors.
ip_list.backend_reaction: Blocked clients receive a warning message page as the HTTP response containing ID: 70007; action options are Alert & Deny (block+log), Deny (no log), or Period Block (1-600 s). Evaluation order is Block IP > Trust IP > Allow Only, before most other scans (performance win). Attack log: 'Blocklisted IP blocked'.

examples.note: Multiple addresses/ranges comma-separated.

examples.pattern-or-value: Block IP: specific IPs; Trust IP: surrounding range
examples.note: Block IP list is scanned first, so specific IPs inside a trusted range can still be blocked.

gotchas: NAT: blocking one source IP may block innocent clients sharing it
Trusted IPs are exempt from many but not all scans (see Sequence of scans)
Ignore X-Forwarded-For moves scanning to TCP layer for performance
Empty Allow Only list = no allow-only screening

geo_ip.what: Blocks traffic by geographic origin using the MaxMind GeoLite region-to-IP database; select countries/territories to block, with an Exception list of IPv4/IPv6 addresses or ranges that are exempted even if inside a blocked region.
geo_ip.backend_reaction: Matching clients are blocked with Alert & Deny (block+log), Deny (no log), or Period Block (1-600 s). Evaluated early in the scan sequence (performance). Known Search Engine source IPs bypass the blacklist.

examples.note: IPv4/IPv6 addresses or ranges added to a named exception item, referenced by the Geo IP rule.

Update the geography-to-IP database periodically (support.fortinet.com)
Ignore X-Forwarded-For option scans at TCP layer for performance
Country list includes territories (Puerto Rico) and non-country regions (Antarctica)

url_access.what: URL access rules accept or deny requests by Host, URL pattern, client source (IP/range, DNS-resolved domain, reverse-DNS source domain), optional parameter checks (with data-type validation), HTTP method and protocol filters. Rules are grouped into a URL access policy; each rule holds multiple conditions with 'meet condition if matches / does not match' logic.
url_access.backend_reaction: Per-rule action: Alert & Deny (block+log, customizable page), Deny (no log), Pass (allow, no log - the default), or Continue (evaluate remaining profile rules; multiple violations produce multiple logs). Attack log message: 'URL Access Violation'. Ignored in Monitor Mode.
regex_fields: URL Pattern when URL Type = Regular Expression
Source Domain when Source Domain Type = Regular Expression
URL Access Parameter Name when Name Type = Regular Expression

Rules at the top of the policy have priority; use Move to reorder (ID does not affect priority)
Does not see RPC traffic - use HTTP Protocol Constraints for RPC
Reverse DNS lookups can hang - set Reverse DNS Timeout
Default severity Low, default action Pass

custom_access.what: Advanced access control ('Custom Policy'/'Custom Rule'): combines filters - source IP, user (needs User Tracking), HTTP method, URL, HTTP header (string/regex, missing-header, empty-value, reverse match), access rate limit, signature-violation category, Geo IP, parameter, transaction timeout, HTTP response code, content type, packet interval timeout, time period, and occurrence thresholds - into one rule; rules are grouped into a Custom Policy with a Threat Weight. Predefined rules (e.g. Vulnerability-Scanning) can be cloned.
custom_access.backend_reaction: On match FortiWeb applies Alert, Alert & Deny, Deny (no log), Period Block (1-3600 s), Client ID Block Period, or Redirect; optional Bot Confirmation first challenges the client (Real Browser Enforcement JavaScript, CAPTCHA, reCAPTCHA/v3, or Mobile Token) and only applies the action if the challenge fails. Attack log: 'Custom Access Violation'. Ignored in Monitor Mode.
regex_fields: HTTP Header name/value when Regular Expression is selected
URL filter accepts a regular expression (e.g. /index\.jsp) or wildcards
HTTP Method Check simple string or regex
Parameter name/value filters

Header Simple String matching is substring ('test' matches 'atest1') and value matching is case sensitive

User filter requires a User Tracking policy in the same profile

dos_protection.what: Application-layer DoS protection: HTTP Access Limit (requests/sec per source IP, with separate Standalone-IP and Shared-IP thresholds), Malicious IPs (TCP connection count per HTTP session cookie), and HTTP Flood Prevention (requests/sec per session per URL); plus network-layer (TCP/IP) rules. Rules are grouped into a DoS Protection policy referenced by the profile; a DoS Protection Exception Policy (client IP / IP group) omits the scans for trusted sources.
dos_protection.backend_reaction: Uses a session cookie to track clients (missing/changed cookie = request dropped); when a rate/connection limit is exceeded FortiWeb applies Alert, Alert & Deny, Deny (no log), or Period Block (1-10000 s for HTTP Access Limit, 1-3600 s otherwise) - Period Block blocks attackers at the IP layer, conserving resources during DDoS. Optional Bot Confirmation (RBE JavaScript/CAPTCHA/reCAPTCHA/mobile token) challenges clients before acting. Attack logs e.g. 'DoS Attack: HTTP Access Limit Violation', 'DoS Attack: Malicious IPs Violation'.

examples.note: Must cover a full page load (HTML + JS + images), else false positives.

Shared-IP threshold ignored unless Shared IP detection is enabled in Advanced settings
Clients must support cookies for session-based counters
After HA failover existing sessions cannot be enforced
Monitor Mode ignores actions
Not all features supported in every operation mode

bot_mitigation.what: Umbrella policy (Bot Mitigation Policy) combining: Known Bots (FortiGuard signatures for malicious bots - DoS/Spam/Crawler - plus Known Good Bots i.e. search engines, and Likely Good Bots), Biometrics Based Detection (mouse/keyboard/touch/scroll events + browser fingerprinting for Headless Chrome/Selenium/PhantomJS, Bot Trait Checking 2-10 traits), Threshold Based Detection (Crawler 403/404 rate, Vulnerability Scanning signature rate, Slow Attack, Content Scraping, Illegal User Scan), and Bot Deception (invisible honeypot link inserted into HTML). An Exception Policy (client IP/host/URI/full URL/parameter/cookie, string or regex, And/Or concatenation) exempts elements from all bot scans.
bot_mitigation.backend_reaction: Known Bots: Alert, Alert & Deny, Deny (no log), Period Block (1-3600 s), Redirect, Send HTTP Response, or Bypass; Known Good Bots skip subsequent scans. Biometrics: Alert / Alert & Deny / Deny (no log) after the JS event-collection window. Threshold detection acts only when Occurrence within the time window is exceeded (e.g. denies the 101st request), then the counter restarts - use Period Block or CLI keep-occurrence-count to extend denial; Crawler also supports Client ID Block Period. Bot Deception: any client requesting the invisible link gets Alert/Alert & Deny/Deny (no log)/Period Block. Bot Confirmation (RBE/CAPTCHA/reCAPTCHA/mobile token) can verify suspected bots before acting.
regex_fields: Biometrics / Bot Deception Request URL when Type = Regular Expression
Threshold Illegal User Scan Request URL (regex with >> validator)
Exception Policy Host/URI/Full URL/Parameter/Cookie values when Operation = Regular Expression Match

Content Scraping applies to text/html, text/plain, xml, soap+xml, json responses

syntax_detection.what: Detects SQL injection by lexing/parsing input into an AST and comparing against built-in standard SQL templates (double-quote, single-quote, as-is injection contexts), and XSS by HTML document parsing + JavaScript compilation (attribute/tag/CSS/function/variable based). Scan targets selectable: Parameter Name, Parameter Value, Request Cookie, User-Agent, Referer, Other Request Header. Virtually eliminates regex-signature false positives/negatives.
syntax_detection.backend_reaction: Per attack-type action: Alert, Alert & Deny, Deny (no log), Send HTTP Response (custom error page), Redirect, or Period Block (1-3600 s; NAT LB X-header caveat). Exceptions (Host/URI/Full URL/Parameter/Cookie, string or regex, And/Or concatenated) skip the scan or can be added straight from the attack log ('Add Exception').
regex_fields: Exception element values: Host, URI (up to 2048 chars), Full URL, Parameter name/value, Cookie name/value when Operation = Regular Expression Match

http_header_security.what: Inserts security response headers into backend responses without code changes: X-Frame-Options (DENY/SAMEORIGIN/ALLOW-FROM), X-Content-Type-Options (nosniff), X-XSS-Protection (Sanitizing/Block Mode), Content-Security-Policy, Feature-Policy/Permission-Policy, Referrer-Policy. Optional URL Filter applies headers only to responses of matching request URLs; an Exception policy excludes specific client IPs and/or request URLs.
http_header_security.backend_reaction: No blocking - matching responses are modified on the wire: the selected header/value is inserted into the HTTP response before it reaches the client.
regex_fields: Request URL when Request URL Type = Regular Expression (rule and exception)

cors.what: Three-part CORS protection: Allowed Origin lists (protocol, domain with wildcards, port, include-subdomains), CORS Protection Rules per host/URL (block all CORS traffic, or restrict by allowed origins, credentials TRUE/FALSE/None, preflight max age 0-86400, allowed methods/headers, exposed headers), and a CORS Protection Policy grouping rules for the inline profile.
cors.backend_reaction: If the Origin matches the allow list FortiWeb permits the request and writes Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <origin> into the response; non-matching or restricted CORS requests are blocked. Attack log: 'CORS Protection Violation'.
actions_available: (allow/deny per rule settings; violations logged as CORS Protection Violation)

If Allowed Origins is left empty the backend decides and may send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * - dangerous with Allowed Credentials TRUE
Allowed Maximum Age applies only to preflighted requests

cookie_security.what: Prevents cookie-based attacks: Security Mode None/Signed (tamper/poisoning detection via hash in the FortiWeb session cookie; needs Client Management)/Encrypted (server cookies transparently encrypted toward clients and decrypted on return); optional Cookie Replay tied to client IP; security attributes added to server Set-Cookies: Cookie Max Age, Secure flag, HTTPOnly flag, SameSite (Strict/Lax/None). Cookie Exceptions table (name + optional domain/path) exempts cookies.
cookie_security.backend_reaction: On violation (tampered, unrecognized/suspicious or replayed cookie): Alert, Alert & Deny, Deny (no log), Remove Cookie (forward the request but strip the cookie before the server), or Period Block (NAT LB X-header caveat). Allow Suspicious Cookies = Never/Always/Custom(date) delays enforcement so pre-existing browser cookies don't cause false positives.

Not supported with a cookie-based Persistence policy unless 'Persistent Cookie' is selected
HTTPOnly may break apps whose scripts read cookies

websocket.what: WebSocket security rules per host/URL: block WebSocket traffic entirely, restrict allowed frame formats (Plain Text/Binary, both on by default), Max Frame Size and Max Message Size (0-2147483647 bytes), Block Extensions (strip/deny the extension header in the handshake), enable attack-signature scanning of message bodies, and an Allowed Origin list (e.g. 121.40.165.18:8800). Rules group into a WebSocket Security Policy referenced under Protocol in the profile.
websocket.backend_reaction: Violations: Alert (accept+log), Alert & Deny (block/reset+log), Deny (no log). Block Extensions + Alert removes the extension field from the packet; + Deny (no log) makes the WebSocket negotiation fail. Signature hits on WebSocket frames can only alert, period-block, or deny - erase/redirect/send-response configured on signatures degrade to alert.
regex_fields: URL when URL Type = Regular Expression (e.g. ^/*.php)

examples.note: Only listed origins accepted; empty list = origin not checked.

gotchas: Attack signature detection not guaranteed when traffic uses an allowed extension header
Signature actions must also be enabled in Known Attacks > Signatures of the same profile
Default action Alert; Block WebSocket Traffic disables all other fields

mitb.what: Man-in-the-Browser protection rules injected into pages: Obfuscation of sensitive input field names (Base64-based disguise so trojans can't find them), Encryption of password parameters (only FortiWeb can decode), Anti-Keylogger for password fields, an AJAX Request allow list (external destinations XHR may contact), and SSL Stripping Detection (Middle Proxy comparison of server response vs client-reported protocol, HSTS enforcement, protocol/header/User-Agent consistency checks). Configured as MiTB protection rules + policy applied in the inline profile.
mitb.backend_reaction: For AJAX requests to external domains not on the allow list FortiWeb takes the configured action (alert, or alert & deny) and can display an alert message in the browser; protected field names/values are rewritten (obfuscated/encrypted) in the served page and transparently restored/decoded by FortiWeb on submission; SSL-stripping mismatches (e.g. client reports http:// for an https:// page) raise alerts.
regex_fields: (rule URL matching per MiTB rule pages; see Creating an MiTB protection rule)

csrf.what: Two lists: Page List (web pages FortiWeb injects JavaScript into) and URL List (requests that must then carry the anti-CSRF token). The injected JS appends parameter tknfv (value = Client Management cookie) to <a href> links and forms; with JS Request Status enabled a second script patches XMLHttpRequest too. Parameter filters (name + value, value regex '*' matches any) disambiguate when page and generated request share the same URL.
csrf.backend_reaction: Requests for listed URLs arriving without tknfv, or with a token not matching the session cookie, trigger Alert (default), Alert & Deny (customizable block page), Deny (no log), or Period Block (1-3600 s).
regex_fields: Full URL when Request Type = Regular Expression (e.g. test\.com instead of full literal URL)
Parameter Value when Parameter Value Type = Regular Expression (enter * to match any value)

padding_oracle.what: Defeats padding-oracle attacks (e.g. Lucky 13) against inputs the application encrypts individually (session IDs, cookies, profile URLs, passwords) with CBC/ECB/OAEP-style ciphers. Rules match Host + Protected URL (string or regex) and specify the Protected Target: URL, Parameter, and/or Cookie.
padding_oracle.backend_reaction: Detects the brute-force guessing pattern and applies Alert (default), Alert & Deny, Deny (no log), or Period Block (1-3600 s; NAT LB X-header caveat). Attack log 'Padding Oracle Attack' may take up to ~2 minutes to appear because of the DoS alert interval (max-dos-alert-interval).

url_encryption.what: Prevents forceful browsing by encrypting matching URLs in server responses so the site's internal directory structure (e.g. /admin, /backups) is never exposed; clients see opaque encrypted URLs and FortiWeb validates/decrypts them on the way back. Rules contain a URL List (Simple String or Regular Expression) and an Exception List; rules group into a URL Encryption Policy in the inline profile.
url_encryption.backend_reaction: Response URLs matching the rule are rewritten to encrypted form; incoming requests whose matching URL is not correctly encrypted are rejected per action: Alert (default), Alert & Deny, Deny (no log), Period Block (1-3600 s). Allow Unencrypted permits valid client requests FortiWeb failed to decrypt.

hidden_fields.what: Protects <input type="hidden"> values (e.g. prices, state tokens) against client-side tampering: FortiWeb caches the hidden-input values served in the page and verifies they are unchanged when the form is POSTed to the listed Post URLs. A Fetch URL tool retrieves the page from a real server and auto-discovers hidden fields and post URLs (color coded: blue add, red remove, black in sync). Rules group into a Hidden Fields Policy.

file_security.what: File Security rules restrict uploads by file type (Allow File Types or Block File Types; content/payload inspection defeats renamed extensions except for 'Whole Suffix Files') and size (File Upload Limit in KB), per Host/URL, with File Uncompress (up to 12 nesting levels / 5000 KB decompressed), JSON-embedded file parsing, and octet-stream filename identification. File Security policies add Antivirus Scan, Signature Detection, FortiSandbox submission, ICAP server scanning, and email attachment scanning (OWA/ActiveSync/MAPI).
file_security.backend_reaction: Violating uploads trigger Alert, Alert & Deny (the default), Deny (no log), or Period Block (1-3600 s). With Hold Session While Scanning File enabled FortiWeb holds the session up to 30 min for FortiSandbox/ICAP verdicts; disabled, it forwards optimistically, then alerts and remembers the malicious file hash for future direct blocking. Ignored in Monitor Mode.

webshell.what: Detects Trojan/web-shell code in uploaded files using two methods: Known Web Shells (tag/keyword signatures) and Fuzzy Hash Based Detection (similarity of the file's hash against a Trojan sample library, so modified scripts are still caught), each split into PHP, ASP, JSP, Perl and Python categories. Individual scripts can be included/excluded per policy.
webshell.backend_reaction: When similarity meets the Fuzzy Similarity Threshold (percentage) or a known web shell matches, FortiWeb applies Alert, Alert & Deny (default), Deny (no log), or Period Block (1-3600 s). Ignored in Monitor Mode.

examples.note: File flagged when similarity >= threshold, regardless of attacker edits.

A validation policy can contain multiple OpenAPI files and is selected in the web protection profile.

api_gateway.what: API user management, API key verification, access control, rate limiting and API call rewriting. API Users (Standard auto-generated key, Dynamic RSA-token, or JWT) with optional IP and Referer restrictions are grouped into API User Groups. API Gateway Rules match Host + frontend URL prefixes (rewritten to backend prefixes), verify the API key from an HTTP header or parameter, restrict to a user group, apply Per-user Rate Limit and global Rate Limit, insert headers, and define Sub-URL rules (method + URL string/regex) with their own key/rate settings.
api_gateway.backend_reaction: On violation (invalid/missing API key, user not in allowed group, rate limit exceeded) FortiWeb applies Alert (default), Alert & Deny, Deny (no log), or Period Block (1-10000 s). X-RateLimit-* headers can be added to responses when the limit is exceeded (limit, remaining, wait time). Matching frontend prefixes are rewritten to backend prefixes before forwarding.

Empty rate limit = unlimited

mobile_api.backend_reaction: Requests without the JWT-token header or with an invalid token trigger Alert (default), Alert & Deny, Deny (no log), or Period Block (1-3600 s).

Rules group into a gRPC Security Policy under Protocol in the profile.

url_rewriting.what: URL Rewriting rules act on requests (rewrite HTTP header: method, Host, URL, Referer; insert/remove up to 10 headers or cookies; rewrite body; 301/302 redirect; Send 403 Forbidden) or responses (rewrite body, Location, status code, insert/remove headers). Conditions match objects (HTTP Host, Request URL, Referer, Body, Location) against regular expressions with 'matches / does not match' logic plus protocol (HTTP/HTTPS) and Content-Type filters. Replacement fields support back-references $0-$9 and variables ($CLIENT_IP, $CLIENT_PORT, $HOST, $URL, $FULL_URL, $UTC_STR, $UTC_INT, $ORIGIN_IP, $VSERVER_IP, $VSERVER_PORT, FortiWeb_PSERVER).
url_rewriting.backend_reaction: When all conditions of a rule match, FortiWeb rewrites the request before forwarding to the server, rewrites the response before returning it to the client, replies itself with a 301/302 redirect (Location supports back-references), or returns 403 Forbidden. Only the first matched rule in the policy executes unless 'Continue Executing the Next Rule' is enabled.

Replacement Host / URL / Location / body Replacement support back-references $0.. to condition capture groups

http_authentication.what: Offloads HTTP authentication/authorization to FortiWeb for sites lacking their own: local user accounts or remote LDAP/RADIUS/NTLM/KDC (Kerberos)/SAML/TACACS+ queries, grouped into user groups; authorization rules bind a user group to a realm and URL set; rules group into an authorization policy selected in the inline protection profile. Auth styles: basic, digest (local users only), NTLM.
http_authentication.backend_reaction: If a request lacks an Authorization: header FortiWeb itself replies 401 Authorization Required with WWW-Authenticate (style + realm); the browser prompts the user and repeats the request with credentials; FortiWeb validates them (locally or against the auth server) and then authorizes each request against the rules; authentication failures (and optionally successes) can be logged/alerted.

user_tracking.what: Tracks sessions by application user: a User Tracking rule defines the Authentication URL, Username/Password fields, Session ID name (e.g. PHPSESSID, JSESSIONID or an API token) and login-success conditions (Return Code / Response Body / Redirect URL, string or regex); captured usernames appear in traffic/attack logs and feed the Custom Policy 'User' filter. Extras: Session Fixation Protection (erases pre-auth session IDs), Limit Concurrent Users Per Account (1-128), Session Timeout with Session Timeout Enforcement + Session Freeze Time, and Credential Stuffing Defense (FortiGuard spilled-credential DB + optional online check with Test button).

Log messages: 'Session Timeout Enforcement: triggered by user <username>.' and 'Triggered by user <username>: Credential Stuffing Defense Violation.' Tracking stops at the Log Off URL or after Session Timeout.

threat_scoring.url: https://docs.fortinet.com/document/fortiweb/7.6.4/administration-guide/... (Policy > Client Management: 'Configuring client management'; see also /704981/threat-weight-configuration-enhancements-7-6-3)
threat_scoring.what: Client Management threat scoring: every security violation carries a Threat Weight (six risk levels Informational/Low/Moderate/Substantial/Severe/Critical, weights 1-500, adjusted per security module in the Threat Weight tree, some modules per-policy); FortiWeb accumulates each client's threat score (client identified by a generated client ID from cookie or source IP) over a Statistics Period and classifies it trusted / unidentified / suspicious / malicious against configured score thresholds (e.g. 0-120 trusted, 121-300 suspicious, >301 malicious).
threat_scoring.backend_reaction: When a client's accumulated score crosses the suspicious/malicious thresholds, Block Settings apply: Alert (accept+log), Alert & Deny (block/reset+log), Block Period (block by source IP for N seconds), or Client ID Block Period (block by FortiWeb client ID, resilient to changing source IPs). With Signature Only Threat Score enabled, single signature hits no longer act individually - action fires only when the signature score threshold is reached ('Always Record Signature Attack Log' controls per-hit logging).

wpp.what: The Web Protection Profile bundles every WAF feature (signatures, access control, API protection, bot mitigation...) into one object a Server Policy binds. Each dropdown names a separate reusable sub-policy.

Clone a shared profile before adding policy-specific exceptions to it.

regex_guide.flavor: FortiWeb follows most Perl-compatible regular expression (PCRE, pcre.org) syntax. Matching is case-sensitive unless you turn on case-insensitivity with (?i). Inverse string matching is NOT supported (you cannot write !(hamsters)); only character-class negation like [^A] is available. FortiWeb evaluates a specific location starting at its beginning and takes only the first match unless repetitions are defined.
notes: Back-reference numbering starts at 0: use $0 (or /0) for the FIRST capture group, not $1. Valid range $0-$9.

$0..$9 = capture groups of the previous match string (e.g. condition-table match reused in URL rewriting); /0../9 = earlier part of the CURRENT string (e.g. (/(^/)*)/0/0/0/0 for repeated path); $+ = highest-numbered capture group; $& = entire match string.
Capture groups are numbered left to right, outside to inside, top to bottom across the condition table: (a)(b)(c(d))(e) yields $0=a, $1=b, $2=cd, $3=d, $4=e.
In URL rewriting, capture groups are numbered ACROSS all condition-table rows: e.g. condition 1 on HTTP Host (.*) is $0 and condition 2 on HTTP URL ^/(.*)$ is $1.
URL-type regex fields do not require a leading slash, but must match URLs that begin with a slash (e.g. /index.cfm); never include the domain name (configured separately as Host).
Always validate with the >> (test) button, which opens the Regular Expression Validator, to check syntax, unintended matches, and intended matches.
Regex evaluation is computationally expensive - use regular expressions only where necessary and build them with care (see 'Regular expression performance tips').

The matching engine uses UTF-8 character values; for regexes matching HTTP requests use the same encoding as the clients; visually similar characters (Latin C vs Cyrillic С 'confusables') have different code points and need explicit alternatives.
Character ranges match by numeric code point: [@-B] matches UTF-8 code points 40-42 (@AB).
FortiWeb does not support regular expressions that begin with an exclamation point ( ! ) (noted on Parameter Validation).
Some fields allow up to 2048 characters for regex (signature/syntax exceptions URI values).

. matches any single character except \r or \n; ^ and $ match line positions (not characters); + is greedy unless followed by ?, * greedy, *? lazy, ? makes preceding item optional, ?= is lookahead (not included in match), | alternation, {n} / {n,m} repetition counts, [] sets/ranges, \ escapes special characters *.|^$?+\(){}[].
